title: A 20-micrometre contact model did not improve swim coherence prediction in 35 inputs to one leech motor neuron
abstract: In 35 mapped inputs to leech motor neuron DE-3R, a local contact model had 6.2% more error than the other-input mean when it predicted coherence across two swim trials. The whole-input label test gave p = 0.2523. The input's own value from the other trial had 82.2% less error than the mean. Thus, repeatable activity did not give a useful local spatial prediction under this model. The result is specific to one preparation, the released coherence summaries, and the stated model. It does not show that structure has no role in function.

display.caption: Prediction skill across path scales, comparison with earlier activity, and the primary swim label reference. Zero is the other-input mean. One ganglion was tested.
